verdict.rationale: Spline's own docs describe two prompt-driven agents. The 3D editor's AI Agent builds and edits scenes from a description (objects, materials, lighting, animation, interactivity). Hana's AI Agent designs a described screen on the canvas, covering layout, type, colour, effects, states and interactions, which the user can then edit by hand. Prompt-based texture and 3D-model generation add to this. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of output quality, and detail on how well prompt-driven editing of existing designs works.

support.subject: As a designer, I can generate or edit designs from a natural-language prompt — first drafts, layouts, or full mockups the tool actually produces

citations.quote: Hana's **AI Agent** designs for you. Describe a screen and it builds it on the canvas: layout, type, colour, effects, states and interactions.
The AI Agent builds and edits 3D scenes for you. Describe what you want and it does the work through the editor itself
describe a screen and Hana designs it, then edit it by hand
